name: Should I add an island or a peninsula?

mainEntity.name: Should I add an island or a peninsula when changing my kitchen layout?
mainEntity.text: Should I add an island or a peninsula when changing my kitchen layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: An island works best in a kitchen with enough surrounding clearance to move comfortably on every side. It can add prep space, storage, casual seating, and a central gathering point. A peninsula is often the better choice in smaller or narrower kitchens because it gives many of the same benefits while keeping one side attached to a wall or cabinet run. That attachment helps define the kitchen zone and can preserve better traffic flow in tight spaces. In Los Angeles homes, where layouts vary widely, the decision should be based on how people move through the room, where appliances are located, and whether the kitchen needs to connect visually to adjacent living areas. A bad island placement can create bottlenecks and reduce usable space, while a well-placed peninsula can improve function dramatically. The right answer is the one that supports daily cooking, entertaining, and circulation without making the room feel crowded.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose an island if you have enough clearance on all sides and want more flexible prep, seating, and storage. Choose a peninsula if the room is narrower or if you need to define the kitchen without blocking traffic flow. The right choice depends on space, circulation, and how the kitchen is used daily.
